title: Dual notes/audio with labels, optimistic UI, and full color contrast fixes

requirements.summary: Extend frontend Chapter type to support dual notes and audio with labels
acceptanceCriteria: Chapter interface includes notesUrl1, notesLabel1, notesUrl2, notesLabel2, audioLabel1, audioLabel2, audioMimeType2 as optional string fields
chapterMapper.ts correctly maps these new fields from canister response to frontend type without breaking existing fields

file_operations.description: Add optional fields to Chapter interface: notesUrl1, notesLabel1, notesUrl2, notesLabel2, audioLabel1, audioLabel2, audioMimeType2 (all optional strings). These fields support dual notes links and dual audio files with custom admin labels.

Update mapChapter function to map the seven new backend fields (notesUrl1, notesLabel1, notesUrl2, notesLabel2, audioLabel1, audioLabel2, audioMimeType2) from ChapterSnapshot to the frontend Chapter type, ensuring empty strings or undefined values are handled correctly and existing field mappings remain unchanged.

requirements.summary: Add chunked upload utility for second audio slot
acceptanceCriteria: uploadAudioFile2 function exists in audioUploadService.ts
It splits the file into chunks of at most 1.5MB
It calls uploadAudioChunk2 sequentially for each chunk
It calls finalizeAudioUpload2 after all chunks are sent
Progress callback fires with percentage 0–100 during upload
Returns a resolved promise on success and a rejected promise with error message on failure

file_operations.description: Add uploadAudioFile2 function that mirrors the existing uploadAudioFile implementation but calls uploadAudioChunk2 and finalizeAudioUpload2 backend methods for the second audio slot. Split File into 1.5MB chunks, upload sequentially, invoke progress callback (0–100%), and return a promise that resolves on successful finalization or rejects with an error message.

requirements.summary: Expand ChapterForm to support dual notes URLs and dual audio uploads with labels
acceptanceCriteria: ChapterForm shows two notes URL text inputs, each with an optional label text field
ChapterForm shows two audio file upload inputs (accept audio/*), each with an optional label text field
Each audio upload shows its own progress bar, success message, and error message
When editing, chapters with existing audio for slot 1 show 'Audio file uploaded' for slot 1; same for slot 2
On save, audio uploads are performed sequentially after chapter create/update
All notes URL and audio fields are optional — chapter with only title saves successfully
notesUrl1, notesLabel1, notesUrl2, notesLabel2, audioLabel1, audioLabel2 values are passed to createChapter/updateChapter

file_operations.description: Replace single notes URL input with two: notesUrl1 + notesLabel1 (placeholder: 'Notes 1 Label') and notesUrl2 + notesLabel2 (placeholder: 'Notes 2 Label'). Replace single audio upload with two: audio1 file input + audioLabel1 (placeholder: 'Audio 1 Label') and audio2 file input + audioLabel2 (placeholder: 'Audio 2 Label'). Add state for both audio files, labels, progress (0–100%), and success/error messages. Show 'Audio file uploaded' status when editing a chapter with existing audioBlob or audioBlob2. On save: create/update chapter with all six new text fields, then sequentially upload audio1 (via uploadAudioFile) and audio2 (via uploadAudioFile2) if files are selected. Display individual progress bars and status messages for each upload. All fields remain optional.

requirements.summary: Update Notes tab to show named buttons for dual notes links
acceptanceCriteria: Notes tab shows a named button for notesUrl1 using notesLabel1 (fallback: 'Notes 1') when notesUrl1 is present
Notes tab shows a named button for notesUrl2 using notesLabel2 (fallback: 'Notes 2') when notesUrl2 is present
Clicking a named button opens/embeds that specific notes URL
Only available (non-empty) notes links are shown
If no notes URLs are present, the existing empty-state UI is displayed

file_operations.description: In the Notes tab, when chapter has notesUrl1 or notesUrl2, display named buttons (using notesLabel1 or 'Notes 1' / notesLabel2 or 'Notes 2' as labels). Track which notes URL is currently selected. Only render buttons for non-empty URLs. If neither URL is present, show the existing empty-state UI. Pass the selected URL to NotesViewer.

Ensure NotesViewer accepts a notesUrl prop and embeds/displays it in the iframe. No structural changes needed if it already handles arbitrary URLs; verify it works with either notesUrl1 or notesUrl2 passed from ChapterPage.

requirements.summary: Update Audio tab to show named buttons for dual audio slots with binary fetching
acceptanceCriteria: Audio tab shows a named button for audio slot 1 using audioLabel1 (fallback: 'Audio 1') when audio data exists for slot 1
Audio tab shows a named button for audio slot 2 using audioLabel2 (fallback: 'Audio 2') when audio data exists for slot 2
Clicking a named button fetches that slot's binary audio and plays it via AudioPlayer using an object URL
Object URLs are revoked on component unmount
Only available audio slots are shown
Falls back to legacy audioUrl if no binary is stored
Shows 'No audio available' UI if neither binary nor legacy URL is available

file_operations.description: In the Audio tab, when chapter.audioBlob or chapter.audioBlob2 exist, display named buttons (using audioLabel1 or 'Audio 1' / audioLabel2 or 'Audio 2'). Track which slot is currently selected. On button click, fetch the binary via getAudioData (slot 1) or getAudioData2 (slot 2), convert to object URL using URL.createObjectURL, and pass to AudioPlayer. Revoke object URLs on unmount. If neither binary is available but legacy audioUrl exists, fall back to it. If no audio is available at all, show 'No audio available' UI.

Ensure AudioPlayer accepts an audioUrl prop (either object URL or external string) and handles it correctly. No structural changes needed if it already supports arbitrary URLs; verify it works with both object URLs and legacy audioUrl strings.

requirements.summary: Implement optimistic UI updates for chapter save operations
acceptanceCriteria: After clicking Save in ChapterForm, the chapter list in AdminPage updates immediately without waiting for the canister response
If the canister write fails, the chapter list reverts to its pre-save state
An error message is displayed if the canister write fails
Successful saves are confirmed once the canister responds and the cache is officially invalidated/re-fetched

file_operations.description: Update useCreateChapter and useUpdateChapter mutations to implement optimistic updates using TanStack Query's onMutate, onError, and onSettled callbacks. In onMutate: snapshot the current 'chapters' query cache, then optimistically update the cache with the new/edited chapter data. In onError: revert the cache to the snapshot and display an error message. In onSettled: invalidate the 'chapters' query to re-fetch authoritative data from the canister. This makes the chapter list appear to update instantly on save.

requirements.summary: Full color contrast audit and fixes across all components in light and dark mode
acceptanceCriteria: All text across every page and component is clearly visible against its background in light mode
All text across every page and component is clearly visible against its background in dark mode
No button, card, tab, form, quiz option, or flashcard face has text that blends into or disappears against its background color
Tailwind dark: variant classes are used for all dark mode color overrides

Fixes apply to Header, Footer, HomePage, ClassPage, SubjectPage, MDCATPage, MDCATSubjectPage, ChapterPage (all tabs), AdminPage, ChapterForm, FlashcardSection, QuizSection, AudioPlayer, NotesViewer, SplashScreen, SupportPage, and TermsPage

Audit and fix text color contrast for page heading, subject cards, PDF entry cards, and any empty-state messages in both light and dark mode. Ensure all text is clearly visible against colored backgrounds using Tailwind dark: variant classes.

Audit and fix text color contrast for page heading, search input placeholder, recently viewed section heading, chapter cards, and empty-state messages in both light and dark mode. Ensure all text is clearly visible using Tailwind dark: variant classes.

Audit and fix text color contrast for empty-state messages, error messages, and 'Open in New Tab' fallback link text in both light and dark mode. Ensure all viewer UI text is clearly visible using Tailwind dark: variant classes.

Audit and fix text color contrast for the splash screen brand text and any tagline/subtitle in both light and dark mode. Ensure splash text is clearly visible against the splash background using Tailwind dark: variant classes.
